Bacteriostatic water for laboratory use: composition, records and limits
Published and updated: 27 August 2026 · Author: PeptidaLab editorial team

Bacteriostatic water is not a peptide. The term is used for certain aqueous solutions that may contain an antimicrobial preservative, commonly benzyl alcohol. Exact composition must not be assumed from the name.
The label and batch dossier should identify composition, preservative concentration, volume, batch, expiry, storage conditions, sterilisation method and relevant testing.
Why no reconstitution instructions are provided
Compatibility depends on the material, method and experimental purpose. Generic instructions may compromise a sample or be misread as guidance for human use.
A container labelled “bacteriostatic” is not automatically authorised for every application. Supplier specifications and legal assessment define permitted use.

What are peptides? Structure, terminology and research context | PeptidaLab EU

Peptides are chains of amino acids connected by peptide bonds. In scientific literature, the boundary between a peptide and a protein depends on context, length, structure and function; no single threshold resolves every case.

The same name may appear in an academic paper, an analytical standard or the documentation of an authorised medicine. These contexts are not equivalent. An RUO material is supplied for controlled experiments and does not acquire the status of a medicine, supplement or cosmetic merely because publications about the molecule exist.

The declared identity, chemical form, molecular mass, analytical method, batch number and validated handling conditions must be assessed together. A name on the label does not replace batch documentation.
How to read a Certificate of Analysis (COA) | PeptidaLab EU
A useful COA must be unambiguously linked to a batch. Check the batch number, date, sample, method, issuing laboratory and the person or system approving the result.

HPLC can describe the chromatographic profile under the conditions of the method used, while mass spectrometry can support molecular-mass verification. Neither method alone justifies every claim about identity, quantity, sterility, endotoxins or suitability for a particular use.

Avoid documents without a batch or method, documents with repeatedly identical results, or those whose issuer cannot be verified. PeptidaLab will not publish percentages or certificates until the documents have been received and validated.
Storing peptide reagents: documentation principles | PeptidaLab EU
Temperature, light, humidity and why the verified batch data sheet takes priority.
There is no single storage instruction that applies to every peptide. Chemical form, formulation, packaging and supplier studies may change the requirements.

Temperature, protection from light and humidity, duration and temperature-excursion limits must be taken from the verified technical data sheet. Generic information found online does not replace product-specific data.
Maintain receipt, monitoring and access logs. Any deviation must be documented and assessed before the material is used in a protocol.
How we evaluate a research-material supplier | PeptidaLab EU
A checklist for identity, traceability, documentation and responsible communication.
How we evaluate a research-material supplier

Assessment begins before an order and continues after receipt. Relevant factors include legal identity, document history, batch consistency, transport conditions and the availability of verifiable technical answers.

Medical promises, self-administration instructions and certificates without traceability are serious risk signals. A responsible supplier states the product’s limits and does not replace uncertainty with spectacular claims.
Retain the acceptance criteria and the reason for the decision. A commercial relationship should not depend on a single PDF or a percentage displayed on a webpage.

Ac-Selank-NH₂ research guide: mechanism, evidence and documentation

appears in the literature in contexts that must be kept distinct: molecular research, preclinical models, possible clinical studies and commercial products. This guide explains the terminology and limitations without dosing, reconstitution or administration instructions.
Declared classification: Acetylated and amidated peptide variant
Status: research use only; availability is confirmed on enquiry

Ac-Selank-NH₂ is an acetylated and amidated variant of the Selank family. It is listed for research on neurobiological pathways associated with stress responses, GABAergic signalling and neuroimmune interactions.

A mention in a scientific paper describes the molecule or model evaluated in that study. It does not automatically confirm the identity, purity, quantity, sterility or suitability of a commercial vial.
Terminal modifications may produce a profile different from unmodified Selank in stability and activity. Variant identity should not be inferred from the family name alone.
Responsible interpretation starts with the species, experimental system, comparator, method and endpoint. In-vitro findings, animal evidence and human-study results are not interchangeable.
Claims concerning anxiety or cognitive performance are not clinical conclusions for this material. Variant-specific and batch-specific data are required.

PeptidaLab does not turn preliminary results into personal promises. Where an authorised medicine uses a similar active substance, that authorisation applies to the specific product, manufacturer, indication and regulated supply chain—not to every material carrying the same name.
What should be verified for the batch?

A useful dossier links the vial unambiguously to its batch number, declared identity, analytical method, quantity, analysis date, issuing laboratory, storage conditions and chain of custody. HPLC and mass spectrometry can answer different questions; no isolated percentage establishes every product characteristic.
Ac-Selank-NH₂ is listed in the catalogue as acetylated and amidated peptide variant. That classification describes a research context, not a medical indication.

MOTS-c and SS-31: two distinct paths in mitochondrial research | PeptidaLab EU

MOTS-c and SS-31 share a broad theme—mitochondrial biology—but they address different questions. MOTS-c is described as a mitochondrial-genome-derived peptide; SS-31, also called elamipretide, is a tetrapeptide designed for mitochondrial association.
Research follows metabolic-stress responses, AMPK-associated signalling and how a mitochondrial-derived peptide may influence gene expression.
For SS-31, hypotheses focus on cardiolipin interaction, inner-membrane organisation and bioenergetics. Results depend on the model and experimental conditions.
A shared theme does not mean a shared mechanism, concentration or interchangeability. Analytical identity, chemical form and protocol must be documented separately.
Both molecules may help frame questions about mitochondrial function, but the evidence does not justify promises for personal use.
Peptide, protein, amino acid and analogue: what is the difference? | PeptidaLab EU

An amino acid is a structural unit. A peptide contains amino acids linked in a chain, while a protein usually has a larger structure and more complex functional organisation. An analogue is a molecule modified to study specific properties or interactions.
Not every product shown alongside peptides is itself a peptide. PeptidaLab therefore separates non-peptide compounds into a distinct category and displays the classification on each product page.
Research peptide prices in Romania: how to compare responsibly | PeptidaLab EU
Research-material prices should be compared using the same molecule, chemical form, quantity and documentation level. Two vials with similar names are not automatically equivalent.
Cost may reflect synthesis or manufacture, independent analysis, packaging, transport monitoring, documentation, taxes and losses from rejected batches.
The cost of an invalid result
A cheap but uncharacterised material can consume laboratory time, reagents and capacity. The real cost includes the risk of repeating the experiment.
Check declared quantity, identity, form, batch, method, laboratory, storage conditions and commercial status. PeptidaLab displays recommended prices but blocks ordering until checks are complete.
Price is a criterion, not evidence. A sound comparison puts documentation and protocol suitability ahead of promotional percentages.
Retatrutide vs Tirzepatide: mechanism and evidence-stage differences | PeptidaLab EU

Retatrutide and tirzepatide are often compared because both affect more than one metabolic pathway, but they are not the same molecule and do not share the same development status. Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist; retatrutide is investigated as a triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon agonist.
Why does the third receptor matter?
The glucagon component is investigated for its effects on energy flux and hepatic metabolism. It changes the pharmacological profile and prevents a simple comparison based on one outcome.
A responsible comparison checks the population, duration, comparator, endpoint, statistical analysis and attrition. Results from separate trials are not a direct head-to-head experiment.
Clinical data for a pharmaceutical product do not validate the identity or quality of an RUO vial. Every PeptidaLab batch requires its own documentation and legal assessment.
The comparison is useful for understanding dual and triple signalling, not for personal recommendations. PeptidaLab provides no dosing, administration or treatment claims.
Semax, Selank and DSIP in neurobiological research: evidence and uncertainty | PeptidaLab EU

Semax, Selank and DSIP are often grouped under labels such as “cognitive” or “sleep”, but that commercial grouping oversimplifies the literature. Each has a different sequence and experimental history.
Preclinical research explores neuromodulation, expression of selected factors and behavioural responses. Ac-Semax-NH₂ and Ac-Selank-NH₂ must not be confused with unmodified sequences.
DSIP is a nonapeptide described in historical studies with heterogeneous results. The name does not establish a predictable effect or replace material characterisation.
Models, species, methods and endpoints differ. Claims about human memory, focus, anxiety or sleep cannot be inferred directly from preclinical experiments.
These materials are relevant as experimental tools only when identity and study design are clear. They are not presented for self-administration.
Batch traceability and the chain of custody | PeptidaLab EU
Traceability links the physical product to the supplier, documentation, receipt, storage and distribution. A code printed on a vial is useful only when it can be reconciled with genuine records.
A coherent system retains the supplier identity, shipping documents, receipt date, quantity, batch, monitored conditions, analytical results and the history of release to the customer.
Public documents may protect commercially sensitive information, but they should not conceal the elements needed to verify authenticity and the link to the batch.
